To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 3D body posture estimation from multi-view images can be achieved by combining the output of multiple 2D pose detectors; 2) multi-view human action and activity recognition is still a challenging task, but the state of the art is improving; and 3) 3D human pose estimation from multi-view videos can be achieved with a reasonable accuracy by applying a 3D pose tracker.
multi-view camera setups have the potential to improve human 3D action recognition and body pose estimation accuracy.

(i) the most promising multi-view human action datasets for 3D pose and action estimation are IXMAS, i3DPOST, and UT-Kinect; and (ii) the most promising approaches for multi-view human pose estimation and action recognition are the approaches by Aggarwal and Ryoo, and the approach by Weinland, which is the only method to date that has been able to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy for multi-view human activity recognition.

the development of methods for 3D human pose estimation and action recognition from multiple views.
the development of multi-view systems for 3D body tracking, human action recognition and human–computer interaction.

multi-view human action and 3D pose recognition is an active research area and there are many open problems that still need to be tackled.

the multi-view camera setup is a promising approach for human 3-D pose estimation and action recognition, but there is a need for a more detailed analysis and comparison of the methods in order to understand the strengths and weaknesses of the approaches, and to be able to identify the key challenges in the area.
, in order to achieve accurate results for 3D human pose estimation and action recognition from multiple views, a combination of the different approaches is necessary.

multi-view approaches have a high potential to overcome the limitations of monocular approaches.
multi-view camera setups can be used to obtain 3D pose estimates and human action recognition results which are superior to those obtained by using a single camera.
there is no one-size-fits-all approach to human 3D body tracking.
